description:
Question: once a self call keeps its caller's key at a supplied slot (fz-sc8.124), is the subtraction in return_flow_mask (src/compiler2/jobs/keying.rs, the .filter(|position| !rebuilt.contains(*position)) line) redundant, so the rule can live in one place?

Measured on 943c9dedf (fz-sc8.124) with the line removed: activation-key COUNTS are identical across 627 fixture backend dumps (19806 keys both ways, no per-fixture change, no exit-code change). Key CONTENT changes in 43 fixtures: at a supplied slot the column reads empty_list() (the outside caller's seed) where it read the collapsed class list(a_e). Examples: 00386 partition/4[.., list(int), list(a2_e), list(a3_e)] -> [.., empty_list(), empty_list()]; 00183 Enum.reverse_list/2[list(int), list(a1_e)] -> [list(int), empty_list()]. One lib pin fails on it: compiler2_quicksort_root_closes_with_a_finite_recursive_frontier (drive_test.rs:14135) expects [a2_e] and gets [].

So the subtraction is not redundant as the tree stands: it is what makes a supplied slot's key column say 'any list' instead of the seed. Deleting it needs a decision on what a key should show at a supplied slot (the seed, or the freight class), and then either the quicksort pin's wording changes or the subtraction stays. The builder reverted; nothing is committed. Evidence: spike scratchpad build124/ (corpus dumps for both binaries). Proposal: /Users/j5n/Workspace/optionparser-compile-cost.html
title: The returned axis no longer subtracts recursion-supplied positions
